key_insight: PathoS2VD generates pseudo z-stacks from single 2D pathology images, enriching tissue representations with plausible cross-plane morphology rather than reconstructing physical 3D tissue.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support computational prostate cancer classification using routine pathology images without dedicated volumetric imaging.
method: Train an image-to-video latent diffusion model on pathology z-stacks to learn z-axis morphological priors.
Generate a pseudo z-stack from a single 2D histopathology image.
Use prior-preserving mixture fine-tuning to adapt to new domains while retaining learned z-axis priors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports realistic cross-plane continuity and consistent prostate cancer classification improvements over 2D representations, but provides no dataset sizes or numerical results.
watch_item: Generated planes are plausible synthetic morphology, not verified tissue anatomy, so classification gains should not be interpreted as validated 3D reconstruction or clinical readiness.
paper_title: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations
